input.description: Telemetry shows a single transient spike to 121°C at 14:15 that reverted to baseline (~89.5°C) at the very next reading 10 minutes later, with coolant_level_pct steady at 96% throughout the entire window (no drop before, during, or after). Service history shows no recent coolant issues (last flush was routine, 3+ months ago). KB search returned two conflicting entries: KB-001 attributes transient spikes with no sustained temp rise to a sensor calibration glitch (fix: restart_sensor), while KB-002 attributes sustained spikes correlated with low coolant level to an actual leak (fix: schedule_service_visit). Since coolant level never dropped and the spike was a single isolated reading rather than sustained, the evidence matches KB-001's pattern, not KB-002's. Recommending restart_sensor as the more evidence-supported option, but flagging the KB conflict for visibility -- if the spike recurs or coolant level begins dropping, a service visit should be scheduled instead.
